newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan construction loans fall for 16th month.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan construction loans fall for 16th month.

text.p: Loans extended by Taiwan banks to construction firms fell 18.54 percent to T$391.62 billion in August from August 1995, marking the 16th consecutive month of negative growth, the central bank said on Monday.
August's decline followed a 17.42 percent fall in July.
In the wider picture, loans extended by Taiwan banks to all private businesses fell 4.95 percent to T$2.894 trillion in August from a year earlier, the central bank announced.
August's overall decline was the fifth monthly decline in 10 years, and all of those were in 1996, the statement said.
Lending fell 0.35 percent in January, 0.80 percent in May, 1.1 percent in June and 2.21 percent in July, it said.
The central bank official attributed the flat-to-negative recent growth to an overall slowing in the economy.
Banks have been particularly cautious in granting loans to companies in the construction sector, which has seen deep recession since the local real estate market peaked in 1989.
In late August, the central bank scrapped all of the selective credit controls on land to boost the real estate market and the economy, and analysts had expected the move to gradually show effect.
